events.title: Node.js 22 released
events.summary: [Node.js] 22.0.0 shipped on April 24, 2024 with require() of ES modules, WebSocket client, and [V8] 12.4.
events.about: [Node] 22 became [LTS] in October 2024 — experimental `require(esm)` eased migration from CommonJS to modules; built-in WebSocket client reduced dependency on `ws`. Native ESM loading via require() became default in [Node] 22.12.0 (December 2024).

narrative.whyChosen: [Node] 22 simplified the ESM/CommonJS interop pain that blocked upgrades.
narrative.whyImportant: Native WebSocket and module loading reduced [npm] surface area for servers.
narrative.problemSolved: Dual package ecosystems forced awkward loaders and bundler workarounds.

events.title: Meta Llama 3 released
events.summary: Meta released [Llama] 3 on April 18, 2024 — open-weight 8B and 70B models with improved [reasoning], coding, and multilingual support.
events.about: [Llama] 3 closed much of the gap with closed APIs like [GPT]-4 and Claude — fueling local [inference] tools (Ollama, LM Studio) and [fine-tuning] pipelines. The 405B variant followed later, but the April release reset expectations for open-model quality.

narrative.whyChosen: [Llama] 3 made frontier-class open weights the default choice for self-hosted AI.
narrative.whyImportant: Competitive open models reduced vendor lock-in for startups and researchers.
narrative.problemSolved: [Llama] 2 lagged closed models on [reasoning] and code — limiting offline deployments.
